'''André Lichnerowicz''' ({{IPA|fr|ɑ̃dʁe liʃneʁɔvits}}; January 21, 1915, [[Bourbon-l'Archambault]] – December 11, 1998, [[Paris]]) was a French [[Differential geometry and topology|differential geometer]] and [[Mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]]. He made pioneering contributions to the theory of the scalar curvature, holonomy groups,  Kähler geometry, and  the mathematical study of Einstein's equations. He also made contributions to symplectic geometry, and is considered the founder of modern [[Poisson geometry]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Revuz|first1=André|last2=Berger|first2=Marcel|last3=Choquet-Bruhat|first3=Yvonne|last4=Marle|first4=Charles-Michel|date=1999|title=Andre Lichnerowicz (1915-1998)|url=https://smf.emath.fr/node/27584|journal=Gazette des Mathématiciens|language=French|volume=82|pages=90–108}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Revuz|first1=André|last2=Berger|first2=Marcel|last3=Choquet-Bruhat|first3=Yvonne|last4=Marle|first4=Charles-Michel|last5=Bourguignon|first5=Jean-Pierre|date=1999|title=Andre Lichnerowicz (1915-1998)|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/199911/mem-lichnerowicz.pdf|journal=Notices Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=46|issue=11|pages=1387–1396}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kosmann-Schwarzbach|first=Yvette|date=2009|title=Tribute to André Lichnerowicz (1915–1998)|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200902/rtx090200244p.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=56|issue=2|pages=244–246}}</ref>

==Biography==
Lichnerowicz's grandfather Jan fought in the Polish resistance against the [[Prussia]]ns. Forced to flee Poland in 1860, he finally settled in France, where he married a woman from [[Auvergne (province)|Auvergne]], Justine Faure. Lichnerowicz's father, Jean, held teaching credentials ([[agrégation]]) in classics and was secretary of the [[Alliance française]], while his mother, a descendant of paper-makers, was one of the first women to earn the agrégation in mathematics. Lichnerowicz's paternal aunt, Jeanne, was a novelist and translator known under the pseudonym {{Interlanguage link|Claude Dravaine|lt=Claude Dravaine|fr}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=André Lichnerowicz - Biography|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Lichnerowicz/|access-date=2021-07-23|website=Maths History|language=en}}</ref>

André attended the [[Lycée Louis-le-Grand]] and then the [[École Normale Supérieure]] in [[Paris]], gaining agrégation in 1936. After two years, he entered the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] (CNRS) as one of the first researchers recruited by this institution.

Lichnerowicz studied [[differential geometry]] under [[Élie Cartan]]. His doctoral dissertation, completed in 1939 under the supervision of [[Georges Darmois]], was entitled "''Problèmes Globaux en Mécanique Relativiste''" (Global problems in relativistic mechanics).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=André Lichnérowicz - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=91104|access-date=2021-07-23|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>

His academic career began under the cloud of [[Nazi Germany|Nazi]] occupation, during [[World War II]]. In 1941 he started teaching at the [[University of Strasbourg]], which was moved to [[Clermont Ferrand]] and only returned to [[Strasbourg]] in 1945, after the end of the war. In November 1943 he was arrested during a raid but managed to escape. During 1944 he was invited to give a [[Peccot Lectures|Cours Peccot]] at the [[Collège de France]].

From 1949 to 1952 he held a position at the [[University of Paris]], and in 1952 he was appointed professor at the [[Collège de France]], where he worked until his retirement in 1986.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Biographie|url=https://www.college-de-france.fr/site/andre-lichnerowicz/|access-date=2021-07-23|website=www.college-de-france.fr|language=fr}}</ref>

Lichnerowicz served as president of the [[Société mathématique de France]] during 1959.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-10-24|title=Anciens Présidents {{!}} Société Mathématique de France|url=http://smf.emath.fr/content/anciens-presidents|access-date=2021-07-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161024023304/http://smf.emath.fr/content/anciens-presidents|archive-date=2016-10-24}}</ref> He was elected member of several national and international academies: the [[Accademia dei Lincei]] in 1962, the [[French Academy of Sciences|Académie des Sciences]] in 1963, the [[Real Academia de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales|Real Academia de Ciencias]] in 1968,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Académicos Históricos - Real Academía de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales|url=https://rac.es/sobre-nosotros/miembros/academicos-historicos/correspondiente-internacional/|access-date=2021-07-23|website=rac.es}}</ref> the [[Académie Royale de Belgique]] in 1975, the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]] in 1981,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Germain|first=Paul|date=2000|title=Commemoration of academicians - André Lichnerowicz|url=http://www.pas.va/content/dam/accademia/pdf/sv99/sv99.pdf|journal=Science and the Future of Mankind|publisher=Pontificiae Academiae Scientiarum Scripta Varia|volume=Proceeding of the Jubilee Plenary Session 10–13 November 2000|pages=40–43|isbn=88-7761-075-1|access-date=23 July 2021|archive-date=16 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191116170648/http://www.pas.va/content/dam/accademia/pdf/sv99/sv99.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the {{Interlanguage link|Accademia delle Scienze di Torino|lt=Accademia delle Scienze di Torino|it}} in 1984.<ref>{{Cite web|title=André LICHNEROWICZ|url=https://www.accademiadellescienze.it/accademia/soci/andre-lichnerowicz|access-date=2021-07-23|website=www.accademiadellescienze.it}}</ref>

In 1988 he was awarded the [[Prix de la langue française]] for having illustrated the quality and the beauty of [[French language]] in his works.<ref>{{Cite web|title=André Lichnerowicz|url=https://www.prix-litteraires.net/detail_prix_auteur.php?auteur=1207_Andre_Lichnerowicz|access-date=2021-07-23|website=www.prix-litteraires.net|archive-date=2021-07-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210723214448/https://www.prix-litteraires.net/detail_prix_auteur.php?auteur=1207_Andre_Lichnerowicz|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2001 he received posthumous (together with his co-authors [[Alain Connes]] and [[Marco Schutzenberger]]) the Peano Prize for his work ''Triangle of Thoughts.''<ref>{{Cite web|title=Premio Peano {{!}} Associazione Subalpina Mathesis|date=3 November 2015 |url=https://www.associazionesubalpinamathesis.it/premio-peano/|access-date=2021-07-23|language=it-IT}}</ref><ref>[[Alain Connes]], "Biographical Note: André Lichnerowicz," in ''Triangle of Thoughts'', 173&ndash;5.</ref>

In 2008 the [[André Lichnerowicz Prize]] was created to reward progresses in [[Poisson geometry]], a research field where Lichnerowicz made pioneering contributions.

Lichnerowicz was a believing Catholic<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.casinapioiv.va/content/accademia/en/academicians/deceased/lichnerowicz.html|title = Andre Lichnerowicz}}</ref> who served as vice-president of the Centre Catholique des Intellectuels Français.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.openedition.org/pur/8739|isbn = 9782753524286|title = Les intellectuels catholiques dans la société française : Le Centre catholique des intellectuels français (1941-1976)|chapter = Chapitre 9. Des années riches de promesses|series = Histoire|date = 24 February 2015|pages = 181–199|publisher = Presses universitaires de Rennes}}</ref>

== Research ==
In an interview in his last years, Lichnerowicz self-described his research interests as "Differential geometry and global analysis on manifolds", "the relations between mathematics and physics" and "the mathematical treatment of Einstein's theory of gravitation".<ref>{{Cite book|last=Schmitt|first=Marian|title=Hommes de science : 28 portraits|date=1990|publisher=Hermann éditeurs des sciences et des arts|isbn=978-2-7056-6124-3|location=Paris|oclc=804198208}}</ref> Indeed, his works contributed, among others, to many areas of [[Riemannian geometry]], [[symplectic geometry]] and [[general relativity]].

His research in general relativity began with his PhD thesis, where he described necessary and sufficient conditions for a [[Riemannian metric|metric]] of hyperbolic [[Metric signature|signature]] to be a global solution of the [[Einstein field equations]]. In a series of papers in 1940 with Raymond Marrot, he provided a mathematical formulation of the relativistic kinetic theory.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lichnerowicz|first1=André|last2=Marrot|first2=Raymond|date=1940|title=Remarques sur l'équation intégrodifferentielle de Boltzmann|journal=C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris|language=French|volume=210|pages=391–393|zbl=0023.32302|url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k31623/f391.item}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lichnerowicz|first1=André|last2=Marrot|first2=Raymond|date=1940|title=Propriétés statistiques des ensembles de particules en relativite restreinte|journal=C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris|language=French|volume=210|pages=759–761|zbl=0024.37704|url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k31623/f759.item}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lichnerowicz|first1=André|last2=Marrot|first2=Raymond|date=1940|title=Sur l'équation intégrodifferentielle de Boltzmann|journal=C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris|language=French|volume=211|pages=531–533|zbl=0024.31804|url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3163d/f531.item}}</ref> He later worked on [[Gravitational Radiation|gravitational radiation]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lichnerowicz|first=André|date=1960-12-01|title=Ondes et radiations électromagnétiques et gravitationelles en relativité générale|journal=Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata|language=fr|volume=50|issue=1|pages=1–95|doi=10.1007/BF02414504|s2cid=183813776|issn=1618-1891|doi-access=free}}</ref> spinor fields,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lichnerowicz|first=André|date=1964|title=Champs spinoriels et propagateurs en relativité générale|url=https://www.numdam.org/item/?id=BSMF_1964__92__11_0|journal=Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France|language=fr|volume=92|pages=11–100|doi=10.24033/bsmf.1604|doi-access=free}}</ref> and propagators<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lichnerowicz|first=André|date=2018-10-16|title=Republication of: Propagators, commutators and anti-commutators in general relativity|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s10714-018-2433-x|journal=General Relativity and Gravitation|language=en|volume=50|issue=11|article-number=145|doi=10.1007/s10714-018-2433-x|bibcode=2018GReGr..50..145L|s2cid=125130979|issn=1572-9532|url-access=subscription}}</ref> on [[Curved space time|curved space-time]], obtaining results which preluded his later works on quantisation and deformation.

Among his contributions to Riemannian geometry, in 1944 he formulated a conjecture about locally harmonic 4-manifolds,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lichnerowicz|first=André|date=1944|title=Sur les espaces riemanniens complètement harmoniques|url=https://www.numdam.org/item/?id=BSMF_1944__72__146_0|journal=Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France|language=fr|volume=72|pages=146–168|doi=10.24033/bsmf.1359|doi-access=free}}</ref> which has been later generalised and is now known as [[Lichnerowicz conjecture]]. In 1952 he showed, together with [[Armand Borel]], that the restricted [[holonomy group]] of a [[Riemannian manifold]] is [[Compact space|compact]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Borel|first1=Armand|last2=Lichnerowicz|first2=André|date=1952|title=Espaces riemanniens et hermitiens symétriques|journal=C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris|language=French|volume=234|pages=2332–2334|zbl=0046.39803|url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3186w/f2332.item}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Borel|first1=Armand|last2=Lichnerowicz|first2=André|date=1952|title=Groupes d'holonomie des variétés riemanniennes|journal=C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris|language=French|volume=234|pages=1835–1837|zbl=0046.39801|url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3186w/f1835.item}}</ref> He proved the now standard equivalence of the various definitions of [[Kähler manifold]] and he worked on the classification of compact [[Homogeneous space|homogeneous]] [[Kähler manifold|Kähler]] spaces.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lichnerowicz|first=André|date=1953|title=Espaces homogènes kählériens|journal=Colloques Internat. Centre Nat. Rech. Sci.|language=French|volume=52|pages=171–184|zbl=0053.11603}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lichnerowicz|first=André|date=1990|title=Groupes kähleriens|journal=Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I|language=French|volume=310| issue =  9|pages=671–676|zbl=0706.22006}}</ref> In 1958 he was one of the first to introduce a relation between the [[Spectrum (functional analysis)|spectrum]] of the [[Laplace operator|Laplacian]] and the [[Curvature of Riemannian manifolds|curvature]] of the metric.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lichnerowicz |first1=André |title=Géométrie des groupes de transformations |journal=Travaux et Recherches Mathématiques |year=1958 |volume=3 |publisher=Dunod, Paris |language=fr |oclc=911753544|mr=124009|zbl=0096.16001}}</ref> After formalising [[Élie Cartan|Cartan]]'s and [[Hermann Weyl|Weyl]]'s theory of [[spinor]]s in a rigorous framework, he proved in 1963 the [[Lichnerowicz formula]] relating the [[Dirac operator]] and the [[Laplace–Beltrami operator]] acting on spinors.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lichnerowicz|first=André|date=1963|title=Spineurs harmoniques|url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k4007z/f7.item|journal=C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris|language=French|volume=257|pages=7–9|zbl=0136.18401}}</ref> By combining this formula 
with the newly-proved 
[[Atiyah-Singer index theorem]], he then proved the unexpected result that 
that many compact simply-connected spin manifolds (including the 4-manifold [[K3 surface|K3]]) do not admit Riemannian metrics of positive scalar curvature, thereby founding an important area of Riemannian geometry that remains active today.<ref>Perspectives in Scalar Curvature, edited by [[Mikhael Gromov (mathematician)|M. Gromov]] and [[H. Blaine Lawson|H.B. Lawson, Jr.]], vols. 1 & 2, World Scientific, 2025.</ref>

In the 1970s his interests turned to symplectic geometry and dynamical systems, with many pioneering papers which, in the next decades, would give rise to the modern field of [[Poisson geometry]]. Indeed, starting in 1974, together with Moshé Flato and Daniel Sternheimer, Lichnerowicz formulated the first definitions of a [[Poisson manifold]] in terms of a [[bivector]], the counterpart of a (symplectic) [[Differential form|differential 2-form]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Flato|first1=Moshé|last2=Lichnerowicz|first2=André|last3=Sternheimer|first3=Daniel|date=1974|title=Déformations 1-différentiables d'algèbres de Lie attachees à une variété symplectique ou de contact|url=|journal=Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série A|language=French|volume=279|pages=877–881|zbl=0289.53031}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Flato|first1=Moshé|last2=Lichnerowicz|first2=André|last3=Sternheimer|first3=Daniel|date=1975|title=Déformations 1-différentiables des algèbres de Lie attachees à une variété symplectique ou de contact|url=https://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1975__31_1_47_0/|journal=Compos. Math.|language=French|volume=31|pages=47–82|zbl=0317.53039}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Flato|first1=Moshé|last2=Lichnerowicz|first2=André|last3=Sternheimer|first3=Daniel|date=1976|title=Algèbres de Lie attachees à une variété canonique|url=|journal=J. Math. Pures Appl. |series=9e Série|language=French|volume=54|pages=445–480|zbl=0318.53041}}</ref> He showed later that the same philosophy can be used to generalise [[contact structure]]s to [[Jacobi manifold]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lichnerowicz|first=André|title=Les variétés de Jacobi et leurs algèbres de Lie associees.|journal=J. Math. Pures Appl. |series=9e Série|language=French|volume=57|pages=453–488|zbl=0407.53025}}</ref> In a 1976 paper one can already find the classical formula <math>[df,dg]=d\{f,g\}</math> for the [[Lie algebroid]] bracket of <math>T^*M</math> on exact 1-forms via the [[Poisson bracket]] of functions.<ref>{{Citation|last=Lichnerowicz|first=André|chapter=Variétés Symplectiques, Variétés Canoniques, et Systèmes Dynamiques|date=1976|chapter-url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/B978012602850850011X|title=Topics in Differential Geometry|pages=57–85|publisher=Elsevier|language=fr|doi=10.1016/b978-0-12-602850-8.50011-x|isbn=978-0-12-602850-8|access-date=2021-07-24|chapter-url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 1977 Lichnerowicz introduced the operator defining what is now called [[Poisson manifold#Poisson cohomology|Poisson cohomology]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lichnerowicz|first=André|date=1977-01-01|title=Les variétés de Poisson et leurs algèbres de Lie associées|journal=Journal of Differential Geometry|volume=12|issue=2|doi=10.4310/jdg/1214433987|issn=0022-040X|doi-access=free}}</ref> His 1978 papers on the [[Deformation (mathematics)|deformation]] of the algebra of smooth functions on a Poisson manifold established the new research area of [[Deformation quantization|deformation quantisation]].<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1978-03-01|title=Deformation theory and quantization. I. Deformations of symplectic structures|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0003491678902245|journal=Annals of Physics|language=en|volume=111|issue=1|pages=61–110|doi=10.1016/0003-4916(78)90224-5|issn=0003-4916|last1=Bayen|first1=F.|last2=Flato|first2=M.|last3=Fronsdal|first3=C.|last4=Lichnerowicz|first4=A.|last5=Sternheimer|first5=D.|bibcode=1978AnPhy.111...61B|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1978-03-01|title=Deformation theory and quantization. II. Physical applications|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0003491678902257|journal=Annals of Physics|language=en|volume=111|issue=1|pages=111–151|doi=10.1016/0003-4916(78)90225-7|issn=0003-4916|last1=Bayen|first1=F.|last2=Flato|first2=M.|last3=Fronsdal|first3=C.|last4=Lichnerowicz|first4=A.|last5=Sternheimer|first5=D.|bibcode=1978AnPhy.111..111B|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Lichnerowicz published more than 350 papers and supervised 24 [[Ph.D.]] students.<ref name=":0" /> A collection of scientific contributions from several of his collaborators was published in his honour in occasion of his 60th birthday.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-94-010-1508-0|title=Differential Geometry and Relativity: A Volume in Honour of André Lichnerowicz on His 60th Birthday|date=1976|publisher=Springer Netherlands|isbn=978-94-010-1510-3|editor-last=Cahen|editor-first=M.|location=Dordrecht|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-94-010-1508-0|editor-last2=Flato|editor-first2=M.}}</ref> In 1982 a personal selection of his own works was published by [[Éditions Hermann|Hermann]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Lichnerowicz|first=André|title=Choix d'œuvres mathématiques|date=1982|publisher=Hermann|isbn=2-7056-5946-3|location=Paris|oclc=9555359}}</ref>

== Pedagogy of mathematics ==
While pursuing an active research career, Lichnerowicz had a deep interest in [[mathematics education]] and [[pedagogy]]. From 1963 to 1966 he was President of the [[International Commission on Mathematical Instruction]] of the [[International Mathematical Union]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Búrigo |first1=E. Z. |title=Researching the History of Mathematics Education: An International Overview |date=2018 |publisher=Springer |chapter=Real Numbers in School: 1960s Experiments in France and Brazil |isbn=9783319682945 |page=30 |editor-first1=Fulvia |editor-last1=Furinghetti | editor-first2=Alexander |editor-last2= Karp |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GZxBDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Historical Sketch of ICMI {{!}} International Mathematical Union (IMU)|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icmi/organization/historical-sketch-icmi|access-date=2021-07-24|website=www.mathunion.org}}</ref> In 1967 the French government created the ''Lichnerowicz Commission'' made up of 18 teachers of mathematics. The commission recommended a curriculum based on [[set theory]] and [[logic]] with an early introduction to [[mathematical structure]]s. It recommended introduction to [[complex number]]s for seniors in high school, less computation-based instruction, and more development from premises (the axiomatic approach). These reforms have been called [[new math|New Math]] and have been repeated internationally.<ref name=":02">{{Cite book |last=Mashaal |first=Maurice |title=Bourbaki: A Secret Society of Mathematicians |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |year=2006 |isbn=0-8218-3967-5 |language=French |translator-last=Pierrehumbert |translator-first=Anna |chapter=10: New Math in the Classroom}}</ref> However, the reforms faced stern backlash from parents, who had trouble helping their children with homework,<ref name=":18">{{Cite news |last=Knudson |first=Kevin |date=2015 |title=The Common Core is today's New Math – which is actually a good thing |work=The Conversation |url=https://theconversation.com/the-common-core-is-todays-new-math-which-is-actually-a-good-thing-46585 |access-date=September 9, 2015}}</ref> teachers, who found themselves ill-prepared and ill-equipped,<ref name=":22">{{Cite web |last=Gispert |first=Hélène |title=L'enseignement des mathématiques au XXe siècle dans le contexte français |url=http://culturemath.ens.fr/histoiredesmaths/htm/Gispert08-reformes/Gispert08.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170715164210/http://culturemath.ens.fr/histoire%20des%20maths/htm/Gispert08-reformes/Gispert08.htm |archive-date=July 15, 2017 |access-date=November 4, 2020 |website=CultureMATH |language=FR}}</ref> and scholars from various disciplines, who deemed the New Math to be simply unsuitable and impractical.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Feynman |first=Richard P. |author-link=Richard Feynman |year=1965 |title=New Textbooks for the 'New' Mathematics |url=https://calteches.library.caltech.edu/2362/1/feynman.pdf |journal=Engineering and Science |volume=XXVIII |issue=6 |pages=9–15 |issn=0013-7812}}</ref><ref name="Kline2">{{cite book |last=Kline |first=Morris |title=Why Johnny Can't Add: The Failure of the New Math |title-link=Why Johnny Can't Add |publisher=[[St. Martin's Press]] |year=1973 |isbn=0-394-71981-6 |location=New York |pages=17, 98 |author-link=Morris Kline}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Simmons |first=George F. |title=Precalculus Mathematics in a Nutshell: Geometry, Algebra, Trigonometry: Geometry, Algebra, Trigonometry |publisher=[[Wipf and Stock Publishers]] |year=2003 |isbn=9781592441303 |page=33 |chapter=Algebra &ndash; Introduction |author-link=George F. Simmons |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dN1KAwAAQBAJ&pg=PA33}}</ref> Lichnerowicz resigned and the commission was disbanded in 1973.<ref name=":22" /> Nevertheless, the influence of the proposed reforms in mathematics education had endured, as the Soviet mathematician [[Vladimir Arnold]] recalled in a 1995 interview.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lui |first=S.H. |date=1995 |title=An Interview with Vladimir Arnold |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199704/arnold.pdf |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=44 |issue=4 |pages=432–8}}</ref>
